STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plates are 20-30 cm; this looks like a medium square side/dinner plate, around 22-24 cm across the diagonal-oriented width.
b) Reference: almonds are 2.3 cm. The plate spans roughly 9-10 almond lengths across its widest extent (about 420 px wide, with an almond about 40-45 px long), so width ≈ 9.5 x 2.3 ≈ 22 cm.
Reconciled width: 22 cm (square, so area = 22² = 484 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Almonds are countable. Visible count: roughly 42 almonds on the surface, with a loose pile 1-2 pieces deep. Adding hidden ones beneath, estimate about 50 almonds total.
- Grams = 50 x 1.2 g = 60 g.
- Check via footprint: the almond cluster covers roughly 25% of the plate (about 120 cm²), with thickness about 2 almonds (≈ 1.5 cm mound average). Volume ≈ 120 x 1.0 cm = 120 ml; almond bulk density ~0.6 g/ml gives ~72 g. Count method (60 g) is the trusted cue; use about 60-65 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer visible; the almonds sit directly on the plate, so no extra items.

STEP 5 - Energy: almonds, raw/roasted, about 580-610 kcal per 100 g; use 600.
Energy ≈ 62 g x 6 kcal/g ≈ 370 kcal.
